messages.text: Investigate how US refineries changed their production mix in 2026 using EIA Today in Energy. Give a concise answer, the reported findings and their explanation with sources. Distinguish reporting periods from publication dates. Use observations from the retrieved reports only; do not invent demand forecasts or claim exhaustive coverage.

9 of 9 claim(s) are supported by retrieved evidence and independently confirmed; 0 have conflicting evidence and 0 are unsupported.

Supported findings:
- U.S. refineries shifted their production mix away from gasoline toward distillate fuel oil and jet fuel in 2026 through August, as higher margins encouraged middle-distillate production.
- EIA published its production-mix report on November 5, 2026; the underlying Petroleum Supply Monthly data extended through August 2026.
- Gasoline refinery yields averaged less than 45% from January through August 2026 and were below the five-year low in every month.
- Distillate fuel oil yields generally exceeded the previous year's levels and were above the five-year average in every reported month.
- The fleetwide average jet fuel yield exceeded 12% for the first time in March 2026 and remained at or above 12% through August.
- EIA attributed the shift away from gasoline, despite high gasoline prices, to constrained global distillate and jet fuel supplies that made their refining margins significantly higher.
- In a separate report published October 22, 2026, EIA said U.S. refinery utilization averaged more than 95% between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998.
- EIA said tight global distillate supplies and high international demand for U.S. distillate exports largely drove the elevated refinery runs.

0 demand scenario(s), 0 supplier link(s) and 0 financial observation(s) are on the canvas.

Research support only — not investment advice. Scenarios are conditional on their stated assumptions, not predictions, and every figure is as of its stated date.

claims.text: EIA published its production-mix report on November 5, 2026; the underlying Petroleum Supply Monthly data extended through August 2026.

links.quote: In-brief analysis November 5, 2026 Refineries have shifted production away from gasoline to middle distillates

Data from our latest Petroleum Supply Monthly—which includes data through August 2026—indicate refinery yields of gasoline have decreased significantly this year to support increased production of distillate fuel oil and jet fuel, sometimes referred to as middle distillates due to their relative cut points in the oil refining process.

claims.text: Gasoline refinery yields averaged less than 45% from January through August 2026 and were below the five-year low in every month.

links.quote: From January through August 2026, refinery yields of gasoline have averaged less than 45% and have been well below the five-year low in every month.

claims.text: Distillate fuel oil yields generally exceeded the previous year's levels and were above the five-year average in every reported month.

links.quote: Conversely, yields of distillate fuel oil have generally been higher than last year and have been above the five-year average in every month.

claims.text: The fleetwide average jet fuel yield exceeded 12% for the first time in March 2026 and remained at or above 12% through August.

links.quote: The U.S. refinery fleet exceeded an average jet fuel yield of 12% for the first time in March 2026, according to EIA data. Since then, the fleetwide average jet fuel yield has remained at or above 12% through the latest Petroleum Supply Monthly data for August 2026.

claims.text: EIA attributed the shift away from gasoline, despite high gasoline prices, to constrained global distillate and jet fuel supplies that made their refining margins significantly higher.

links.quote: Despite high gasoline prices, refinery yields of motor gasoline have trended below the five-year (2021–2025) low throughout 2026. This decline largely reflects refinery efforts to shift as much of their yields as possible into the production of distillate fuel oil and jet fuel, where margins are significantly higher because of constrained global supplies for these fuels.

claims.text: In a separate report published October 22, 2026, EIA said U.S. refinery utilization averaged more than 95% between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998.

links.quote: In-brief analysis October 22, 2026 U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026

The U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998.

claims.text: EIA said tight global distillate supplies and high international demand for U.S. distillate exports largely drove the elevated refinery runs.

links.quote: This year the refinery runs were driven largely by tight global supplies for distillate fuel oil, leading to high international demand for U.S. distillate fuel oil exports.

claims.text: The gasoline finding describes a smaller production share per barrel processed; it does not by itself establish a decline in gasoline production volume.

links.quote: Petroleum refinery yields represent the share of a specific fuel that is produced from each barrel of crude oil a given refinery (or group of refineries) processes.
From January through August 2026, refinery yields of gasoline have averaged less than 45% and have been well below the five-year low in every month.
